_provenance: Recorded 2026-11-04 by probes/record_vobsub.py on a throwaway, unclaimed Plex Media Server 1.42.2.10156-f737b826c (plexinc/pms-docker, the build plexscratch42 runs) on zen, given a route out for its codec downloads; the listings and the four-language collapse were checked on plexscratch42 itself, over its loopback hop with its .LocalAdminToken, in a Personal Media (tv.plex.agents.none) movie library: offline, the Plex Movie agent adds no local subtitle at all, and a PMS that cannot download its transcoder's codecs answers every conversion's playlist 500 ('Decoder install failed: h264'). Each title is a generated 120 s 1920x1080 black h264 + AAC .mkv, made byte-unique (PMS takes same-hash files for one part), with real VobSub pairs beside it read unchanged off releases through fun's zurg: Samurai Champloo E20's forced track (STARS, inside the release's RAR under Subs/; 1,245 B idx, 28,672 B sub, `id: de`), The 100 S02E01's forced track (RSG, loose, named for the group not the video; 1,380 B / 36,864 B, `id: de`) and McBain (HD4U, loose; 84,745 B / 12,879,872 B, da fi no sv in one pair; listed as four streams until the part is analysed, then as one, the first's id with the last's language, reproduced on plexscratch42 with PUT .../analyze). `Vobsub Embedded` is the clip with Champloo's pair muxed in by mkvmerge (dvd_subtitle, ger, zlib), `Vobsub Text Controls` an embedded SRT and ASS and the `.en.srt`/`.fr.ass` in `files`. `streams`: every subtitle's key read bare and with each extension, with and without `encoding=utf-8` (as Plezy asks), each body by length and which file it is (else its digest); `decisions`: each client's own conversion request (subtitles_s1422.json's rows) with that stream selected, the start answer and the segment at the first cue: its streams, its lit frames (the video is black) and, for a burn, how far the first lit frame is from FFmpeg's own rendering of each of the .idx's tracks; Plex Web's direct-play request (decision_stream_language_zen.json's) too.
